knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Working from the top down means the cleaner never walks on a wet surface that others must use.
Dry soil left on treads turns into a film when damp mopped, so it is removed first.
A contained liner stops soiled pads from dropping grit back onto the treads.

practicalCriteria: Chooses a backpack vacuum or dust mop for dry soil and works from the top down.
Damp mops each landing with a clean pad and bags each used pad in the liner.
Places signs at both ends while the stairs are wet and keeps the route clear.
passRule: Knowledge checks: 80 per cent pass mark, so all three must be correct. The practical sign-off is separate, observed by an assessor, and is not shown by a quiz result.
evidenceRequired: Observed practical sign-off on assessor sheet
Job record or photo of the finished area
stopWorkCriteria: Wet treads left without signs, or people on the flight during damp mopping
Cord with a missing earth pin or damaged insulation used
Bucket and vacuum carried together on the stairs
